## What you will build

Over five days you move from a raw PDHS `.DTA` file to a published, reproducible
report. Not five disconnected topics — one pipeline, assembled a piece at a time.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### The analytical arc

1. **Import & wrangle** survey data that arrives messy
2. **Explore** it with tables and charts that survive peer review
3. **Model** it, with weights, and map it
4. **Report** it in Quarto — parameterised, so it re-runs next year
5. **Accelerate** all of the above with AI assistants you can actually trust
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### What you need

- R ≥ 4.3 and [Positron](https://positron.posit.co) (or RStudio)
- Quarto ≥ 1.4
- The workshop data pack (`data/`)
- No prior R required — Day 1 starts from zero

See [Setup](setup.qmd) before Day 1.
:::

:::

## How the material is organised

Each day folder holds three kinds of file:

- `index.qmd` — the session plan for that day
- `NN-*.qmd` — slides and walkthroughs, in teaching order
- `scripts/*.R` — the live-coding scripts, runnable on their own

Every script resolves data with `here::here("data/...")`, so you can run any script
from anywhere in the project without changing your working directory.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Working alongside the facilitator
Open the project by double-clicking `d4d.Rproj`. That sets the project root, which
is what `here::here()` anchors to. Opening a loose `.R` file instead will break paths.
:::
